name: ARGENTINA

flag.title: Sol de Mayo
flag.note: Blue & white bands; golden Sun of May

lead: Argentina stretches from steamy jungle in the north to icy Patagonia in the south — six climate zones in one country. Home to thundering Iguazú Falls, tango, giant glaciers, and the highest peak outside Asia. Argentines sip bitter mate at all hours, grill enormous steaks, and cheer for football with a passion that shakes entire cities.
geo: Argentina is the world's eighth-largest country. The Andes mountains run the entire western edge like a spine. To the east lie the flat, grassy Pampas — perfect for cattle. In the far south, Patagonia is a cold, windy plateau peppered with glaciers.

Iguazú Falls in the north — nearly 275 separate cascades — is wider than any other waterfall on Earth. Far south, Ushuaia is the world's most southerly city, so close to Antarctica that cruise ships stop there before heading to the frozen continent.
animals: The capybara, Earth's biggest rodent, can weigh as much as a large dog and loves paddling in Argentina's Iberá wetlands alongside caimans. The giant anteater shuffles through the same marshes, slurping up 35,000 ants a day with its sticky tongue.

Patagonia's Atlantic coast hosts the world's largest Magellanic penguin colony at Punta Tombo — over a million birds nest every spring. Guanacos (wild relatives of the llama) roam the windy steppe in thousands, sometimes running faster than a car on a quiet road.
culture: Tango was born in the port neighbourhoods of Buenos Aires in the 1880s, blending African rhythms with European waltzes. Today couples dance it on street corners and in candlelit milonga halls every night of the week.

The asado (barbecue) is practically a religion — Argentines grill beef for hours over wood embers with family and friends. Mate, a bitter herbal tea sipped through a metal straw, is shared in a communal gourd as a sign of friendship.
history: Humans reached the tip of Patagonia about 13,000 years ago. The Inca Empire pushed south into northwest Argentina in the 1400s, but most of the country was home to many independent peoples when Spanish explorers arrived in 1516.

Argentina declared independence on 9 July 1816 — still celebrated as a national holiday. General José de San Martín then crossed the Andes to free neighbouring Chile and Peru, becoming one of South America's greatest liberating heroes.
wows: Argentina made the world's first animated feature film — 'El Apóstol' — in 1917.
Buenos Aires has more psychoanalysts per person than any other city on Earth.
Argentina's national sport, El Pato, is a horseback game mixing polo and basketball.
The first-ever public radio broadcast was made from a Buenos Aires rooftop in 1920.
Aconcagua (6,959 m) is the tallest peak in the Western and Southern Hemispheres.
A Titanosaur found in Patagonia may be the largest dinosaur ever discovered.
A baby was born at an Argentine Antarctic base in 1978 — the first Antarctic-born person.

myths.myth: Argentina is one big beef farm
myths.fact: Argentina is hugely varied — Mendoza makes world-class wine, Misiones has dense jungle, and Patagonia looks more like Iceland than a cattle ranch.
Early tango was considered scandalously wild — banned in schools and condemned by the Pope before becoming the beloved art form it is today.
